current_bottleneck: Flexible exact one-step transition likelihood improves local marginal increment density and average coverage, but it still does not produce coherent free-running joint paths. Cross-cell dependence, h1 mean reversion, per-cell/regime coverage allocation, level occupancy, and pathwise jump balance remain broken.
last_result_summary: 625a implemented and trained a conditional RealNVP transition likelihood over joint38 empirical-score increments. It scored 3/11 on the broad-frame IV bridge: surface, block-AR, and cointegration passed; coverage, conditionality, time-series, regime coverage, distributional fidelity, cross-cell correlation, mean reversion, and pathwise jump realism failed. Metrics: cov90 81.6%, conditionality MAE reduction 4.2%, turb/calm ratio 1.099, daily KS 22/25, level KS 4/25, median-bias 11/25, persistent undercoverage 7.2%, cross-cell corr/rank 0.426/2.658, mean-reversion ratio 0.684, pathwise KS 0.534.
next_step_recommendation: Run a post-experiment synthesis of 610-625 before any new code. Do not sweep RealNVP coupling depth, scale clip, or temperature yet. Decide whether a clean learned-law route remains locally plausible, or whether the risk-manager-deployable route should be reframed as a base native joint law plus disclosed scenario-set/risk-policy calibration.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 610a is the cleanest native joint learned law so far because it generates IV and anchor factors through one shared AR transition model.
